input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: process critique: a records-based 'what did recent runs of my track do' tool (platform/ci/recent_runs.py)

doc_friction.issue: Backlog held only owner rows again. The top live friction candidates I checked were all fixed already: check_post_frontmatter (reports every problem and exits 1), cite_check ancestor caches, run_workflow_locally standalone-checks-first, pick_track's claimed-programme skip. Took ~6 checks to find an unfixed one. The measure table could hide reports older than the newest commit touching that file.

~25 run records on 2026-11-12/13 say post front-matter caps (title 110, description 60-160, seo_title 70) are learned only by failing a check. `check_post_frontmatter.py --limits` exists, but no always-read file names it. Every place a run is told to write a post is control plane (goals.md 'Write about the work', CLAUDE.md), so this PR could not fix it.

Its recent-ideas check (and creative/prompt-0.md's git log -15 spread check) should point at `platform/ci/recent_runs.py --track <t>`. That is a control-plane edit, so it is left to an owner-approved PR.

deviations.why: Critique mode suggests filing new problems in prompts/process/backlog/, but that directory is control plane and would hold this PR for owner approval.
deviations.did: Recorded the gated findings (front-matter caps line, prompt pointers to recent_runs.py) in doc_friction instead.
deviations.result: PR stays mergeable without the owner.

notes: Critique lens: duplicate work and the shallow-clone recency checks. Main health 62/62 green. Measured over 3 days: 858 records, 35 same-track pairs on one project within 20 min (ventures 24, polish 4, creative 3, research 2, perf 1, quality 1), an upper bound on duplicate work. The first recent_runs reading found #15319/#15320, two creative runs on one proposal 2 min apart. Review stall (2674/40 counter) is the known stale-claim issue; owner-gated PR #14686 fixes it. Backlog ids touched: none (all open rows are owner-owned).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: survey friction, write and test a 150-line CLI, measure, write post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
